title: Disney's Moana Remake Earns $177 Million Worldwide but Braces for Major Loss
excerpt: The live-action Moana has crossed $177 million globally after two weekends, but with a $250 million production budget and steep drops, Deadline estimates Disney could lose $100–125 million on the film.
body:
• Disney's live-action Moana has earned $177.3 million worldwide after two weekends — $81 million domestic and $96.3 million international.
  • Deadline estimates Disney could lose between $100 million and $125 million on the film, which cost $250 million to produce before marketing.
  • The remake's 31% Rotten Tomatoes score and 56% second-weekend domestic drop put it among the weakest Disney live-action adaptations alongside Snow White and Dumbo.
  • The underperformance raises fresh questions about Disney's remake-heavy strategy and Dwayne Johnson's drawing power as a leading man.

Disney's live-action Moana has crossed $177.3 million at the global box office after two weekends in theaters — a number that would be respectable for most films but amounts to a commercial disaster for a movie that cost $250 million to produce.

The film, starring Dwayne Johnson as the demigod Maui and newcomer Catherine Laga'aia as Moana, opened to just $43 million domestically and $52 million overseas on its debut weekend of July 10–12, according to Box Office Mojo. Those figures fell well short of Disney's pre-release forecast of $60–65 million domestic and roughly $140 million global.

A Steep Second-Weekend Slide

Things worsened in week two. Moana collected $19 million in its second domestic weekend, a 56% decline that dropped it behind Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey for the top spot in North America. Internationally, the film added $25 million, down 52.2% from its opening. The cumulative totals now stand at $81 million domestic and $96.3 million international, according to The Numbers.

Deadline Hollywood has projected that the film could ultimately lose Disney between $100 million and $125 million, factoring in production costs and an estimated $120 million global marketing spend. The original animated Moana cost roughly $150 million to make and earned $684 million worldwide; its 2024 sequel, Moana 2, crossed $1 billion. The live-action version is tracking toward a lifetime total of $275–300 million — nowhere near enough to break even.

Critics and Audiences Diverge

Review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes has the film at a 31% critics' score, with Metacritic assigning it a 42 out of 100. The New York Times' Alissa Wilkinson called it "the most pointless, and perhaps not accidentally, the worst" of Disney's live-action remakes. Polygon's Tasha Robinson wrote that "virtually every line, beat, and song in the new movie is identical to the 2016 version" and that "there's no artistic or aesthetic reason for this movie to exist."

Audiences who did show up were more forgiving. CinemaScore exit polls gave the film an A- grade, suggesting that the negative reaction lives more in the decision not to buy a ticket than in the theater itself.

Disney's Remake Problem

Moana's struggles place it alongside Snow White, which debuted to $42.2 million in 2025 and finished its run at $205.7 million against a budget exceeding $270 million, and 2019's Dumbo, which opened at $46 million. The underperformance sits in stark contrast to Lilo & Stitch, the live-action adaptation that earned over $1 billion just last year.

Multiple factors explain the gap. Moana arrived just 10 years after the beloved original and less than two years after Moana 2, making it difficult to generate event-level excitement. It also landed in a crowded July marketplace alongside Disney's own Toy Story 5, which has earned $879 million globally. Variety attributed the poor showing partly to "fatigue" from Disney's remakes and competition from within the studio's own slate.

"Disney is bracing for a loss of at least $100 million on the big-budget remake."

— Variety, Box Office Analysis

Questions About Star Power

The result also intensifies scrutiny of Dwayne Johnson's box office pull. Johnson was Hollywood's top-paid performer in 2024, earning a reported $88 million, according to the New York Post. But his recent track record outside voice roles has been uneven: Red One (2024) grossed $186 million against a budget exceeding $200 million, while Black Adam (2022) was another commercial disappointment. Moana adds another entry to a pattern that industry observers say challenges the logic of guaranteed star paydays in an era when audiences increasingly choose films over faces.

What's Next

Projections now place Moana's final domestic total between $120 million and $135 million, with a global finish unlikely to exceed $300 million. Disney has not publicly commented on the film's financial outlook, but the result will almost certainly shape decisions about which animated properties get the live-action treatment — and at what price.

For the Indian diaspora audience, Moana's trajectory offers a lens into broader shifts in Hollywood economics. The original animated film became a cultural touchstone in many South Asian and Pacific Islander communities, and Moana 2's billion-dollar run showed the franchise's enduring appeal. Whether the live-action stumble dampens appetite for Disney's upcoming slate — which includes live-action adaptations of Tangled and Hercules — remains an open question.
